title: Winter warmth had a more positive link than spring warmth to the hazel flower-to-leaf gap in four Swiss samples, 1961-2020
abstract: We tested seasonal temperature slopes for the gap between hazel flowering and leaf unfolding at 50 percent. We used 3,982 paired station-years at 92 Swiss stations. Four tests split stations into western and eastern groups and years into 1961-1990 and 1991-2020. The winter-minus-spring slope contrasts were +5.96 to +7.04 days per degree C. All four adjusted intervals were above zero. Equal year weights, station effects and a time trend controlled part of the observation bias. Stricter station coverage, station trends and year-score serial correlation checks kept positive adjusted intervals. This extends a prior cross-species test to two stages within hazel. The result shows different seasonal links, not a causal warming effect or harm to biodiversity. Shared regional weather, coarse temperature data, missing visit logs and possible changes in plants or observers limit inference. Code, a paired evidence table, source hashes, a figure and numerical checks are included. No air pollutant or weather extreme was tested.

display.caption: Winter-minus-spring slopes for the leaf date minus flower date. Bars are four-test adjusted 95 percent intervals. The two regions have different stations. They share regional climate.

citations.reason: Uses the broad region-period design and the same public source files. New code tests two stages within hazel, not the hazel-to-beech gap. Records overlap.
Prior report describes network change, date uncertainty and different shifts in spring stages.
